321	@dataclass(frozen=True)
322	class MerkleProof:
323	    """Frozen, self-contained bundle of one Merkle public key and one signature.
324	
325	    Unlike :class:`MerkleSignature` (whose wire format needs the
326	    corresponding key separately), a proof carries the
327	    :class:`MerklePublicKey` that constrains its :class:`MerkleSignature`, so
328	    it can be transported on its own and verified with :meth:`verify`. The
329	    proof stores no message and is a pure serialisation container: it offers
330	    neither authentication nor encryption of the wrapper itself.
331	    """
332	
333	    public_key: MerklePublicKey
334	    signature: MerkleSignature
335	
336	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
337	        if not isinstance(self.public_key, MerklePublicKey):
338	            raise TypeError("public_key must be a MerklePublicKey")
339	        if not isinstance(self.signature, MerkleSignature):
340	            raise TypeError("signature must be a MerkleSignature")
341	        if not _signature_matches_key(self.signature, self.public_key):
342	            raise ValueError("signature is not consistent with the public key")
343	
344	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
345	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 proof wire format as ``bytes``.
346	
347	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAMPRF\\0"``; one version byte
348	        (1); the public-key and signature lengths as 4 big-endian bytes each;
349	        then the existing v1 encodings of the public key and of the signature
350	        constrained by that key, in that order. Encoding is deterministic: the
351	        same proof always produces the same bytes.
352	        """
353	        if not isinstance(self, MerkleProof):
354	            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a MerkleProof")
355	        key_bytes = self.public_key.to_bytes()
356	        signature_bytes = self.signature.to_bytes(self.public_key)
357	        return (
358	            _PROOF_MAGIC
359	            + bytes((_PROOF_VERSION,))
360	            + len(key_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
361	            + len(signature_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
362	            + key_bytes
363	            + signature_bytes
364	        )
365	
366	    @classmethod
367	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "MerkleProof":
368	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`MerkleProof`.
369	
370	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
371	        ``TypeError``. The embedded public key is recovered first and then
372	        constrains the signature. A bad magic, an unknown version, a length
373	        field that is out of bounds or disagrees with the actual content,
374	        truncation, trailing data, an invalid nested encoding, or a signature
375	        inconsistent with the key (wrong parameters or counts) raises
376	        ``ValueError`` and no half-valid object is returned.
377	        """
378	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
379	            raise TypeError("proof data must be bytes or bytearray")
380	        data = bytes(data)
381	        if len(data) < _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:
382	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
383	        if data[:8] != _PROOF_MAGIC:
384	            raise ValueError("bad proof magic")
385	        if data[8] != _PROOF_VERSION:
386	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported proof version: {data[8]}")
387	        key_length = int.from_bytes(data[9:13], "big")
388	        signature_length = int.from_bytes(data[13:17], "big")
389	        key_end = _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES + key_length
390	        signature_end = key_end + signature_length
391	        if key_length == 0 or signature_length == 0:
392	            raise ValueError("a length field must not be zero")
393	        if key_end > len(data) or signature_end > len(data):
394	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
395	        if signature_end < len(data):
396	            raise ValueError("trailing data after the proof encoding")
397	        public_key = MerklePublicKey.from_bytes(data[_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:key_end])
398	        signature = MerkleSignature.from_bytes(
399	            data[key_end:signature_end], public_key
400	        )
401	        return cls(public_key=public_key, signature=signature)
402	
403	    def verify(self, message: Any) -> bool:
404	        """Verify the embedded signature against the embedded public key.
405	
406	        Accepts ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` exactly like
407	        :func:`merkle_verify`, to which this call delegates; it returns
408	        ``True`` only for the message that was actually signed. The proof
409	        itself carries no message and cannot authenticate its own origin.
410	        """
411	        return merkle_verify(message, self.signature, self.public_key)
412	
413	
414	def _signature_matches_key(signature: MerkleSignature, public_key: MerklePublicKey) -> bool:
415	    """Non-raising check mirroring the constraints enforced by ``to_bytes``."""
416	    try:
417	        w, height, chains = _signature_params(public_key)
418	        index = signature.index
419	        wots_signature = signature.wots_signature
420	        auth_path = signature.auth_path
421	    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
422	        return False
423	    if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
424	        return False
425	    if index >= (1 << height):
426	        return False
427	    if not _nodes_well_formed(wots_signature):
428	        return False
429	    if not _nodes_well_formed(auth_path):
430	        return False
431	    if len(wots_signature) != chains:
432	        return False
433	    if len(auth_path) != height:
434	        return False
435	    return True
436	
437	
438	def _validate_batch_fields(public_key: Any, signatures: Any) -> None:
439	    """Enforce the :class:`MerkleBatchProof` field types and structure."""
440	    if not isinstance(public_key, MerklePublicKey):
441	        raise TypeError("public_key must be a MerklePublicKey")
442	    if not isinstance(signatures, tuple):
443	        raise TypeError("signatures must be a tuple of MerkleSignature")
444	    for signature in signatures:
445	        if not isinstance(signature, MerkleSignature):
446	            raise TypeError("every signature must be a MerkleSignature")
447	    if not signatures:
448	        raise ValueError("signatures must not be empty")
449	    for signature in signatures:
450	        if not _signature_matches_key(signature, public_key):
451	            raise ValueError("signature is not consistent with the public key")
452	    indices = [signature.index for signature in signatures]
453	    if any(former >= latter for former, latter in zip(indices, indices[1:])):
454	        raise ValueError("signature indices must be strictly increasing and unique")
455

457	@dataclass(frozen=True)
458	class MerkleBatchProof:
459	    """Frozen bundle of one Merkle public key and several of its signatures.
460	
461	    The batch generalises :class:`MerkleProof`: every
462	    :class:`MerkleSignature` in ``signatures`` is constrained by the same
463	    :class:`MerklePublicKey`, so the whole batch travels as one
464	    self-contained object and verifies with :meth:`verify`. ``signatures``
465	    must be a non-empty tuple whose leaf indices are strictly increasing
466	    (hence unique). The batch stores no messages and is a pure
467	    serialisation container: it offers neither authentication nor
468	    encryption of the wrapper itself.
469	    """
470	
471	    public_key: MerklePublicKey
472	    signatures: tuple[MerkleSignature, ...]
473	
474	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
475	        _validate_batch_fields(self.public_key, self.signatures)
476	
477	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
478	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 batch wire format as ``bytes``.
479	
480	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAMBAT\\0"``; one version byte
481	        (1); the public-key length as 4 big-endian bytes; the signature
482	        count as 2 big-endian bytes; the complete v1 encoding of the
483	        public key; then, in tuple order, each signature's length as 4
484	        big-endian bytes followed by its existing v1 encoding constrained
485	        by that key. Encoding is deterministic: the same batch always
486	        produces the same bytes. Fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen
487	        constructor raise ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` instead of
488	        producing a malformed encoding.
489	        """
490	        if not isinstance(self, MerkleBatchProof):
491	            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a MerkleBatchProof")
492	        _validate_batch_fields(self.public_key, self.signatures)
493	        if len(self.signatures) > _MAX_BATCH_SIGNATURES:
494	            raise ValueError("the signature count does not fit in 2 bytes")

715	            raise TypeError("checkpoint data must be bytes or bytearray")

724	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported checkpoint version: {body[8]}")

1190	def merkle_verify(message: Any, signature: Any, public_key: MerklePublicKey) -> bool:
1191	    """Recover the W-OTS public key from ``signature`` and climb to the root.
1192	
1193	    The leaf hash is rebuilt from the recovered key, the authentication path
1194	    is folded in according to the bits of ``signature.index`` (leaf level
1195	    first), and the result is compared against ``public_key.root``. A wrong
1196	    public key *type* raises ``TypeError``; every other structural, range or
1197	    content mismatch returns ``False`` — including keys or signatures whose
1198	    fields were corrupted by bypassing the frozen-dataclass constructors.
1199	    """
1200	    if not isinstance(public_key, MerklePublicKey):
1201	        raise TypeError("public_key must be a MerklePublicKey")
1202	    if not isinstance(signature, MerkleSignature):
1203	        return False
1204	    try:
1205	        w = public_key.w
1206	        height = public_key.height
1207	        root = public_key.root
1208	        index = signature.index
1209	        wots_signature = signature.wots_signature
1210	        auth_path = signature.auth_path
1211	    except AttributeError:
1212	        return False
1213	    try:
1214	        _validate_w(w)
1215	        _validate_height(height)
1216	    except ValueError:
1217	        return False
1218	    if not isinstance(root, bytes) or len(root) != ELEMENT_BYTES:
1219	        return False
1220	    if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
1221	        return False
1222	    if not _nodes_well_formed(wots_signature) or not _nodes_well_formed(auth_path):
1223	        return False
1224	    if len(auth_path) != height:
1225	        return False
1226	    if index >= (1 << height):

1228	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
1229	    if len(wots_signature) != l1 + l2:
1230	        return False

1232	        digits = _signing_digits(message, w)
1233	    except TypeError:

1236	        _chain_walk(element, b - 1 - digit)
1237	        for element, digit in zip(wots_signature, digits)
1238	    )

1250	) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
1251	    """Canonical sibling coordinates for a multiproof over ``indices``.
1252	
1253	    Starting from the leaf indices at level 0, each level records the sibling
1254	    of every current-set index whose sibling is not itself in the current set,
1255	    then the set is shifted right and deduplicated for the next level. The
1256	    returned coordinates are sorted by level then index — exactly the order the
1257	    v1 wire format uses.
1258	    """
1259	    current = set(indices)

1262	        siblings = {index ^ 1 for index in current if (index ^ 1) not in current}

1268	def multiproof_encode(public_key: Any, signatures: Any) -> bytes:
1269	    """Compress several signatures of one Merkle public key into one proof.
1270

1272	    path is not stored: siblings shared by the selected leaves are deduplicated
1273	    into one canonical node set, so every sibling the verifier cannot itself
1274	    derive is carried exactly once.

1277	    :class:`MerklePublicKey` and ``signatures`` a non-empty tuple of
1278	    :class:`MerkleSignature` — or ``TypeError`` is raised. ``ValueError`` is
1279	    raised for an empty set, leaf indices that are not strictly increasing, a
1280	    signature that the key does not constrain (wrong ``w``/height, an index out

1282	    an auth-path node that disagrees with another signature at the same
1283	    coordinate, or a tree whose shape cannot be expressed in the v1 format
1284	    (more than 65535 leaves or sibling nodes, or a level above 255).
1285

1287	    the public-key length as 4 big-endian bytes; the leaf and sibling-node
1288	    counts as 2 big-endian bytes each; the complete v1 encoding of the public
1289	    key; then, in increasing index order, one block per leaf holding the

1302	            raise TypeError("every signature must be a MerkleSignature")

1311	    if any(isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) for index in indices):

1316	        raise ValueError("a signature index is out of range for the public key's tree")

1318	        if not _nodes_well_formed(signature.wots_signature):
1319	            raise ValueError("a W-OTS signature element is malformed")
1320	        if not _nodes_well_formed(signature.auth_path):
1321	            raise ValueError("an authentication path node is malformed")
1322	        if len(signature.wots_signature) != chains:
1323	            raise ValueError("a W-OTS signature length does not match the chain count")
1324	        if len(signature.auth_path) != height:
1325	            raise ValueError("an authentication path length does not match the tree height")
1326	
1327	    coordinates = _canonical_multiproof_nodes(tuple(indices), height)
1328	    if len(coordinates) > _MAX_MULTIPROOF_NODES:
1329	        raise ValueError("the node count does not fit in 2 bytes")
1330	    node_values: dict[tuple[int, int], bytes] = {}
1331	    for signature in signatures:
1332	        for level in range(height):
1333	            key = (level, (signature.index >> level) ^ 1)
1334	            node = signature.auth_path[level]
1335	            previous = node_values.get(key)
1336	            if previous is not None and previous != node:
1337	                raise ValueError("conflicting authentication nodes at the same coordinate")
1338	            node_values[key] = node
1339	
1340	    key_bytes = public_key.to_bytes()
1341	    parts = [
1342	        _MULTIPROOF_MAGIC,
1343	        bytes((_MULTIPROOF_VERSION,)),
1344	        len(key_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big"),
1345	        len(signatures).to_bytes(2, "big"),
1346	        len(coordinates).to_bytes(2, "big"),
1347	        key_bytes,
1348	    ]
1349	    for signature in signatures:
1350	        parts.append(signature.index.to_bytes(2, "big"))
1351	        parts.append(len(signature.wots_signature).to_bytes(2, "big"))
1352	        parts.append(b"".join(signature.wots_signature))
1353	    for level, index in coordinates:
1354	        parts.append(bytes((level,)))
1355	        parts.append(index.to_bytes(2, "big"))
1356	        parts.append(node_values[(level, index)])
1357	    return b"".join(parts)

1361	    """Verify a :func:`multiproof_encode` proof against one message per leaf.
1362

1365	    usual message rules (``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``). Every W-OTS public
1366	    key is recovered from its message, hashed with the existing leaf rule and
1367	    merged level by level with the existing internal-node rule, consuming each
1368	    proof node exactly once. Verification returns ``True`` only when the merge
1369	    reaches the public-key root and every carried node was used; any other
1370	    outcome — a wrong argument type or count, an illegal message member, a bad
1371	    magic/version/length/count field, truncation, trailing data, a
1372	    non-canonical node coordinate, a missing, extra, duplicated or unordered
1373	    node, or a mismatched message — returns ``False``.
1374	    """
1375	    if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
1376	        return False
1377	    if not isinstance(messages, tuple):
1378	        return False

1380	    if len(data) < _MULTIPROOF_HEADER_BYTES:
1381	        return False

1383	        return False
1384	    if data[8] != _MULTIPROOF_VERSION:
1385	        return False

1387	    leaf_count = int.from_bytes(data[13:15], "big")
1388	    node_count = int.from_bytes(data[15:17], "big")
1389	    if key_length == 0 or leaf_count == 0:
1390	        return False
1391	    if len(messages) != leaf_count:
1392	        return False
1393	    offset = _MULTIPROOF_HEADER_BYTES
1394	    key_end = offset + key_length

1396	        return False
1397	    try:
1398	        public_key = MerklePublicKey.from_bytes(data[offset:key_end])
1399	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
1400	        return False
1401	    w = public_key.w
1402	    height = public_key.height
1403	    root = public_key.root
1404	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
1405	    chains = l1 + l2
1406	
1407	    leaves: dict[int, bytes] = {}
1408	    offset = key_end
1409	    previous_index = -1

1413	        index = int.from_bytes(data[offset : offset + 2], "big")
1414	        element_count = int.from_bytes(data[offset + 2 : offset + 4], "big")

1416	        if index >= (1 << height) or index <= previous_index:
1417	            return False
1418	        previous_index = index

1431	        except TypeError:

1434	            _chain_walk(element, b - 1 - digit)
1435	            for element, digit in zip(wots_signature, digits)
1436	        )

1452	        if previous_coordinate is not None and coordinate <= previous_coordinate:
1453	            return False
1454	        previous_coordinate = coordinate
1455	        proof_nodes[coordinate] = node

1457	        return False

1459	    if set(proof_nodes) != set(_canonical_multiproof_nodes(indices, height)):
